question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $9,$ the additive inverse of $15$ modulo $9$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $15$ modulo $9$ is the integer $0\le x<9$ such that

$$
x+15≡0\,(\text{mod}\,9).
$$

First, we note that $15≡6\,(\text{mod}\,9):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}15 & ≡1\cdot 9+6 & \,(\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡1\cdot 0+6 & \,(\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡6 & \,(\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-6+6≡0,$ so $x≡-6\,(\text{mod}\,9).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-6 & \,(\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡0-6 & \,(\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡9-6 & \,(\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡3 & \,(\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $15$ modulo $9$ is $3.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}15+3≡18≡2\cdot 9≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
